what_changed_today: Price ticked up modestly to 7,483.24 (~flat vs prior 7,483.23) but again failed to reclaim the 23.6% fib (7,498) — the snap-back remains capped ~1.3% below the 6/15 swing high (7,578).
Weak intraday structure persists: after trading up toward ~7,540 the index faded to close in the bottom third of the daily range (7,427.55–7,540.75), a second consecutive distribution-style close.
Monte Carlo down-skew held: prob_down_first 59.6% / prob_up_first 40.4%, still failing all regime thresholds (65/70/75); median days upside 5d vs downside 2d shows a faster path down.

ERP compressed back to ~0.05% (from 0.48% prior) as the 10y rose to 4.485% against forward PE 20.17x — the valuation cushion is essentially gone and the 0.5% re-entry floor (7,442) now sits just below spot.

Credit widened to a junk spread of 1.46% (Extreme Fear) and breadth stayed weak (McClellan ~893, net new highs 1.85%, safe-haven -1.62%) — neither has turned up to confirm the multi-week price recovery.
narrative_summary: A mechanically intact bull skeleton — 50-day above a rising 200-day, price +7.78% over the 200-day, and a benign sub-17 VIX below its 50-day MA — is colliding with a stalling snap-back that has twice failed the 23.6% fib (7,498) and closed weak in the bottom third of its range. Valuation offers no cushion (ERP ~0.05% at the ceiling, forward PE ~20x), breadth remains in Extreme Fear (McClellan ~893, net new highs 1.85%) and credit has widened to 1.46%, so the internals still refuse to confirm the price recovery. Monte Carlo is 59.6% down-first and fails every regime threshold. The justified posture is trim bias into strength and defensive patience — not chasing the rally into resistance.
open_questions: Can price reclaim and hold the 23.6% fib (7,498) after two rejections and press toward the 6/15 swing high (7,578), or does the repeated failure mark the next distribution point?

Will breadth (McClellan ~893, net new highs 1.85%) and credit (junk spread 1.46%) finally turn up to confirm the multi-week price recovery, or does their persistent divergence confirm narrow leadership into resistance?
With ERP back at the ~0.05% ceiling and the 10y rising to 4.485%, does further rate pressure force a valuation-driven fade even if the technical skeleton holds?
